subject: Chemistry
title: The Chemistry of Superglue
description: One-minute skill: The Chemistry of Superglue.

hook.text: Superglue was discovered by accident in 1942. It bonded every surface in the lab—including instruments.

buildup.text: Harry Coover was trying to make clear plastic gun sights. His cyanoacrylate mixture stuck to everything.

discovery.text: Cyanoacrylate polymerizes instantly on contact with trace moisture. Water on any surface triggers the bond.

twist.text: That's why it bonds skin so well—your skin is always slightly moist. It was even used to seal wounds in Vietnam.

climax.text: The bond forms in seconds because water molecules initiate an anionic chain reaction along the surface.

punchline.text: Moisture triggers instant polymerization. Water is superglue's secret.

quiz.question: What triggers superglue to bond?
options: Trace moisture on surfaces initiates polymerization
Heat from friction between the surfaces
Oxygen in the air reacts with the glue

details.summary: Superglue is cyanoacrylate, a monomer that polymerizes almost instantly when exposed to trace amounts of moisture on surfaces. Water molecules initiate an anionic polymerization chain reaction that converts the liquid monomer into long, rigid polymer chains, bonding surfaces together in seconds.
details.whyItMatters: Superglue demonstrates anionic polymerization triggered by ambient moisture, an elegant chemical mechanism that makes it one of the fastest-acting adhesives available.
takeaways: Traces of water on surfaces trigger the polymerization reaction
Cyanoacrylate monomers form rigid polymer chains within seconds
It was discovered accidentally during World War II research

faq.question: Why does superglue bond skin so easily?
faq.answer: Human skin always has a thin layer of moisture that initiates polymerization instantly. The slightly alkaline pH of skin also accelerates the reaction. The large surface area of fingerprint ridges provides excellent contact..

faq.question: Why does superglue not work well on some surfaces?
faq.answer: Superglue requires surface moisture to polymerize. Very dry, smooth, or non-porous surfaces like certain plastics provide little moisture and few bonding points. Acidic surfaces can neutralize the anionic polymerization reaction. The glue also fills gaps poorly because it shrinks during curing.
